transport: official Agent SDK 0.3.322 streaming input; Claude Code CLI 2.1.319

probe.purpose: Find where the CLI places a trailing user message that arrives while an MCP tool handler is parked.
probe.tool: one in-process SDK MCP tool named probe with no arguments; its handler parks until the probe releases it
probe.initial_user_message: Call the probe tool exactly once with no arguments. Then write the exact token that the tool returns.
probe.trailing_user_message: TRAILING_MARKER_9Q: also write the word PINEAPPLE after the token.
cases: before_release: push the trailing user message on the streaming input queue, wait, then release the tool result
after_release: release the tool result, then push the trailing user message

capture_method.primary: The official CLI diagnostic environment variable OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES pointed at a private file directory. It wrote each raw /v1/messages request body and its response. The probe read only the sdk query-source records.
capture_method.why_not_session_log: This agent session has a workspace-write file sandbox. The CLI tried to create the session transcript under ~/.claude/projects and the sandbox refused it with EPERM. The CLI debug log records 'Session file materialize failed (EPERM)' and 'Transcript write failed (EPERM)'. The session-log request records were therefore not available to this probe.

second_request_messages.content: one tool_result block for the probe tool call, with the text TOOL_TOKEN_7Q and no trailing text

The user sent a new message while you were working:
TRAILING_MARKER_9Q: also write the word PINEAPPLE after the token.

This is how Claude Code surfaces messages the user sends mid-turn - within the running turn, often alongside the next tool result, rather than as a separate conversation turn. Address the message above as you continue this turn.

conclusion: To deliver trailing dsh user or context content inside the same native turn, the adapter must send it on the streaming input queue before it releases the tool results.

In that order the CLI adds the content to the same API request as the tool_result, as a CLI-generated system-role mid-turn context message immediately after the tool_result message. It does not put the content inside the tool_result and does not drop it.
The model received both inputs in one turn and answered once.

If the adapter releases the tool result first, the CLI finishes the tool turn before it reads the trailing message. The trailing message then becomes a new user turn with its own model request and answer. One dsh stream cannot represent that correctly.
The adapter must keep the same native session and must not fold the trailing content into the tool result.

implementation_decision.order: queue the trailing user content, then release the tool-result batch
implementation_decision.item: extend the waiting-for-results admission to split the suffix into the leading tool-result batch and the trailing user messages; keep both in the committed dsh transcript
implementation_decision.image_policy: a non-offloaded image in a trailing mid-turn message is refused before native dispatch; this probe measured text only

proven: The official SDK accepts a user message on the streaming input queue while an MCP tool handler is parked.
With trailing input queued before the tool result is released, the CLI delivered both inputs in one native turn and one model request followed the tool result.
The CLI placed the trailing text in a system-role mid-turn message after the tool_result block, not inside the tool_result.
With the opposite order, the CLI ended the tool turn first and started a second native turn for the trailing message.
not_proven: The plugin's own dsh profile path; this probe used the SDK directly.
The CLI session-log request records; this session's file sandbox blocked transcript writes, so raw API bodies from the official diagnostic were used instead.
An image or a structured content block in a trailing mid-turn message.
Several separate trailing messages in one boundary, or the exact message boundaries that the CLI preserves.
Behavior on another CLI or SDK version.
Signed-thinking retention across a mid-turn user message.
